meal.title: Switch Statements and Structs in C
meal.objective: Use a switch statement and define a simple struct

voice.script: What if you could pick a menu option and the program remembers your choice? How do you handle several distinct possibilities without a long chain of if statements? First, a struct is a custom bundle that groups different pieces of data under one name. Here we define a struct named Result that contains an integer called guess and a character array called message. In main we read a number into guess, then a switch statement examines the guess value and jumps to the matching case label. Each case assigns a specific message to the Result and then breaks out of the switch. Finally we print the message stored in the struct. The decision flow looks like a branching diagram, showing the guess leading to different messages. Remember, a switch lets you choose among many constant values, and a struct lets you keep related data together. Try adding a new case for the number five that says 'Perfect!'
